version.changelog:
here-now 1.10.0 is a feature release expanding publishing capabilities.

- Adds support for proxy routes enabling server-side API calls (e.g., LLMs, databases, email, payments) from hosted sites.
- Updates skill description to reflect new ability to "build a chatbot" and connect to external APIs.
- No functional changes to publishing flow, authentication, or API key management.
- Existing static hosting and usage remains unchanged.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.10.0

The 'here-now' skill provides a legitimate utility for deploying static sites and files to the here.now hosting platform. The primary script, scripts/publish.sh, is well-implemented with a specific security guard to prevent the accidental transmission of API keys to non-standard base URLs. While SKILL.md contains explicit instructions for the AI agent to automatically manage its own credentials in ~/.herenow/credentials, this behavior is transparently documented and strictly limited to the service's own authentication tokens. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized remote execution, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are coherent with a static-hosting/publish tool: it only needs an optional here.now API key and reads/writes a local credentials/state file to publish files to presigned URLs.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (publish static files, optional proxy routes) matches the included publish.sh script and API reference. Required tools (curl, file, jq) and optional HERENOW_API_KEY/credentials file are reasonable for this purpose. The script's behavior (create site, upload to presigned URLs, finalize, save local state) is congruent with a hosting client.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to perform the full sign-in flow (request code by email, prompt user for code) and to store the returned apiKey into ~/.herenow/credentials itself (explicitly: 'do not ask the user to run it manually'). This is within the skill's purpose but means the agent will be expected to write credentials and local state to disk and to handle sensitive data (email, one-time code, apiKey). Users should be aware the agent will access and persist these secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automatic installer (instruction-only). The publish script will exit if jq is missing and prints a suggestion to install jq via a remote script (curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash). That suggestion is optional but using a remote shell install is higher risk — the skill itself does not automatically run it, but users/agents may be encouraged to run it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only credential surface is here.now-specific: optional HERENOW_API_KEY, ~/.herenow/credentials, and the local .herenow/state.json cache. No unrelated cloud or system credentials are requested. The number of env/config accesses is proportional to the feature (authenticated vs anonymous publishes).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local files: ~/.herenow/credentials (home) and .herenow/state.json (working directory). It does not request always:true or modify other skills. Persisting an API key to the user's home directory is expected for this tool but is a persistent change the user should consent to.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: publish files via here.now. Before installing/using it, understand that: (1) the agent will ask for your email and a one-time code and may write the returned API key to ~/.herenow/credentials on your machine — only proceed if you trust the here.now service and the agent. (2) Anonymous publishes expire after 24 hours; claim tokens and claim URLs are returned only once, so the agent must save/share them if you want permanence. (3) The script will ask for jq; it prints a suggestion to install jq by piping a remote install script (curl | bash) — avoid running remote install scripts unless you trust the source. (4) Review scripts/publish.sh yourself before allowing any agent to run it or to write files to your home directory. If you prefer not to let an agent write credentials, you can obtain and store the API key manually in ~/.herenow/credentials and run the publish script yourself.
